note: Questions from the CBSE Class XII Chemistry board exam 2026, Q.P. code 56/1/1, published by CBSE at cbse.gov.in. Q1, whose options are graphs, is left out; structural formulae are written as condensed formulae or names. Solutions are written for this portal and are not CBSE's official marking scheme.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: Which of the following solutions will have the lowest freezing point in water?
questions.solution: ΔT_f ∝ i × m. CaCl₂ gives 3 ions (i = 3), the largest depression, so the lowest freezing point.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: Which of the following is not a transition metal?
questions.solution: Hg has a completely filled 5d¹⁰ shell in the atom and in its common ions, so it is not regarded as a transition metal.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: Which of the following represents the fraction of molecules with energies equal to or greater than Eₐ?
questions.solution: The Boltzmann factor e^(−Eₐ/RT) gives the fraction of molecules with energy at least Eₐ.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: What will happen during the electrolysis of an aqueous solution of CuCl₂ using platinum electrodes?
options: H₂ gas will be released at cathode
O₂ gas will be released at anode
Cl₂ gas will be released at anode
questions.solution: Cu is deposited at the cathode, and Cl⁻ is oxidised to Cl₂ at the anode (oxygen has a high overpotential).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: Aspirin is obtained by acetylation of
questions.solution: Acetylation of salicylic acid (2-hydroxybenzoic acid) with acetic anhydride gives acetylsalicylic acid.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: The secondary valency of Co in the complex [Co(NH₃)₅(NO₂)]²⁺ is
questions.solution: Secondary valency equals the coordination number: 5 NH₃ + 1 NO₂ = 6.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: At low temperature, phenol reacts with dilute HNO₃ to yield
questions.solution: Dilute nitric acid at low temperature gives a mixture of o- and p-nitrophenol.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: Which of the following is not true about enantiomers?
options: They have the same chemical reactivity.
They have the same specific rotation.
They have the same melting or boiling point.
They have the same refractive index.
questions.solution: Enantiomers rotate plane-polarised light by equal amounts in opposite directions, so their specific rotations differ in sign.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: Aniline on direct nitration yields
questions.solution: In strong acid much of the aniline forms the anilinium ion (meta-directing), so direct nitration gives about 51% para, 47% meta and 2% ortho products.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: Which of the following amines has the lowest pK_b value?
questions.solution: Lowest pK_b means strongest base. Methyl groups (+I) increase basicity; the nitro group strongly decreases it. N,N-dimethylaniline is the strongest base here.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: The deficiency of which of the following vitamins causes increased fragility of red blood cells and muscular weakness?
questions.solution: Vitamin E deficiency causes increased fragility of RBCs and muscular weakness.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text:
Assertion (A): It is not possible to separate the components of an azeotrope by fractional distillation.
Reason (R): Components of an azeotrope have the same composition in liquid and vapour phase and boil at a constant temperature.
options: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).
Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).
Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.
Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.
questions.solution: Since vapour and liquid have the same composition, distillation cannot change it; R explains A.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text:
Assertion (A): The presence of the –OH group in phenols directs the incoming group to the meta position in the ring.
Reason (R): The –OH group in phenols activates the aromatic ring towards electrophilic substitution reaction.
options: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).
Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).
Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.
Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.
questions.solution: –OH is ortho/para directing, so A is false. It does activate the ring, so R is true.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text:
Assertion (A): Actinoids show a wide range of oxidation states.
Reason (R): Actinoids are radioactive in nature.
options: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).
Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).
Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.
Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.
questions.solution: Both are true, but the range of oxidation states comes from the comparable energies of 5f, 6d and 7s orbitals, not radioactivity.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text:
Assertion (A): The pentaacetate of glucose does not react with H₂N–OH.
Reason (R): It indicates the presence of a free –CHO group in glucose.
options: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).
Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).
Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.
Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.
questions.solution: A is true. It shows the absence of a free –CHO group in the cyclic form, so R is false.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: What type of deviation from Raoult's law is shown by a mixture of phenol and aniline? Give reason. What will happen to the boiling point of the solution on mixing phenol and aniline?
questions.solution: Negative deviation: the phenol–aniline intermolecular hydrogen bonds (O–H···N) are stronger than the attractions in the pure liquids. The vapour pressure falls, so the boiling point rises (a maximum-boiling azeotrope can form).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: Why are haloarenes less reactive towards nucleophilic substitution reaction? Give two reasons.
questions.solution: (1) Resonance gives the C–X bond partial double-bond character, making it harder to break. (2) The carbon is sp² hybridised, so the C–X bond is shorter and stronger. Also, the phenyl cation is unstable, and the electron-rich ring repels the incoming nucleophile.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: Write IUPAC names of the following coordination compounds : (i) [Ag(NH₃)₂][Ag(CN)₂] (ii) K₃[Fe(C₂O₄)₃]
questions.solution: (i) Diamminesilver(I) dicyanidoargentate(I). (ii) Potassium trioxalatoferrate(III).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: (i) Give a chemical test to show that [Co(NH₃)₅SO₄]Cl and [Co(NH₃)₅Cl]SO₄ are ionisation isomers. (ii) What is meant by the 'chelate effect'? Give an example.
questions.solution: (i) With AgNO₃, [Co(NH₃)₅SO₄]Cl gives a white precipitate of AgCl (free Cl⁻); with BaCl₂, [Co(NH₃)₅Cl]SO₄ gives a white precipitate of BaSO₄ (free SO₄²⁻). (ii) Complexes with chelating (polydentate) ligands are more stable than those with comparable monodentate ligands, e.g. [Ni(en)₃]²⁺ is more stable than [Ni(NH₃)₆]²⁺.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: Differentiate between the following : (i) Peptide linkage and glycosidic linkage (ii) Essential amino acids and non-essential amino acids
questions.solution: (i) A peptide linkage (–CO–NH–) joins amino acids in proteins; a glycosidic linkage (C–O–C) joins monosaccharide units in carbohydrates. (ii) Essential amino acids cannot be made by the body and must come from the diet (e.g. valine, leucine); non-essential ones are synthesised by the body (e.g. glycine, alanine).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: The reaction 2A + B → 2C takes place in one step. How will the rate of the reaction change if the volume of the reaction vessel is decreased to one third of its original volume? Will there be any change in the order of reaction with the reduced volume?
questions.solution: Being elementary, rate = k[A]²[B]. Reducing the volume to 1/3 triples each concentration, so the rate becomes 3² × 3 = 27 times. The order (3) does not change.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: For the first order thermal decomposition reaction C₂H₅Cl(g) → C₂H₄(g) + HCl(g), the total pressure was 0.30 atm at t = 0 and 0.50 atm at t = 30 s. Calculate the rate constant. [Given : log 3 = 0.48]
questions.solution: If P₀ = 0.30 atm and x decomposes, total P = P₀ + x, so x = 0.20 and the reactant pressure is P₀ − x = 2P₀ − P = 0.10 atm. k = (2.303/30) log(0.30/0.10) = (2.303/30)(0.48) ≈ 3.7 × 10⁻² s⁻¹.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: Answer the following : (i) Why is the equilibrium constant K_c related to E°cell and not to Ecell? (ii) Two metals A and B have standard electrode potentials −0.24 V and +0.80 V respectively. Which of these will liberate hydrogen gas from dilute H₂SO₄? (iii) Write the cell reaction which occurs in a lead storage battery when it is being charged.
questions.solution: (i) At equilibrium Ecell = 0, and the Nernst equation then gives E°cell = (0.0591/n) log K_c; K_c is fixed by standard conditions. (ii) A, because its reduction potential is below that of hydrogen (0.00 V), so it can reduce H⁺. (iii) 2PbSO₄ + 2H₂O → Pb + PbO₂ + 2H₂SO₄.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: What type of battery is the mercury cell? Why is it more advantageous than a dry cell? Write the overall reaction taking place in the mercury cell.
questions.solution: It is a primary cell. It gives a constant voltage (about 1.35 V) throughout its life because no ions are involved in the overall reaction whose concentration changes. Overall: Zn(Hg) + HgO(s) → ZnO(s) + Hg(l).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: Calculate the boiling point of a solution containing 0.61 g of benzoic acid (molar mass 122 g mol⁻¹) in 5 g of CS₂, in which it dimerises to the extent of 88%. The boiling point and K_b of CS₂ are 46.2 °C and 2.3 K kg mol⁻¹ respectively.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: Write the reactions of D-glucose with the following : (a) HI (b) Br₂ water (c) Conc. HNO₃
questions.solution: (a) Prolonged heating with HI gives n-hexane, CH₃(CH₂)₄CH₃. (b) Bromine water oxidises –CHO to –COOH: gluconic acid, HOOC(CHOH)₄CH₂OH. (c) Nitric acid oxidises both –CHO and –CH₂OH to –COOH: saccharic (glucaric) acid, HOOC(CHOH)₄COOH.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: Give reasons for the following : (a) Carboxylic acids have higher boiling points than alcohols of comparable molecular masses. (b) α-Hydrogens of aldehydes and ketones are acidic in nature. (c) Nucleophilic addition of ammonia and its derivatives does not occur with the carbonyl group in strongly acidic medium.
questions.solution: (a) Carboxylic acids form more extensive hydrogen bonding and exist as dimers. (b) The carbonyl group is electron-withdrawing, and the carbanion (enolate) formed after losing an α-H is resonance stabilised. (c) In strong acid, ammonia and its derivatives are protonated and lose their lone pair, so they can no longer act as nucleophiles.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: Write the reaction involved in the following : (a) Reimer-Tiemann reaction (b) Kolbe's reaction (c) Friedel-Crafts acylation of anisole
questions.solution: (a) Phenol + CHCl₃ + aq. NaOH, then H⁺ → 2-hydroxybenzaldehyde (salicylaldehyde). (b) Sodium phenoxide + CO₂ (4–7 atm, 400 K), then H⁺ → 2-hydroxybenzoic acid (salicylic acid). (c) Anisole + CH₃COCl with anhydrous AlCl₃ → 2-methoxyacetophenone (minor) and 4-methoxyacetophenone (major).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: Compound X with molecular formula C₄H₉Br reacts with aqueous KOH to give an alcohol. The rate of this reaction depends only on the concentration of X. When an optically active isomer Y of X was treated with aqueous KOH, the rate was found to depend on the concentration of both Y and KOH. (a) Write the structural formulae of X and Y. (b) Out of X and Y, which one will undergo racemisation and why? (c) Out of X and Y, which one will form a product with inversion of configuration and why?
questions.solution: (a) X is 2-bromo-2-methylpropane, (CH₃)₃CBr (SN1). Y is 2-bromobutane, CH₃CH(Br)CH₂CH₃ (chiral, SN2). (b) X, as it reacts by SN1: the planar carbocation intermediate is attacked equally from both faces, which leads to racemisation (X itself is achiral, so its product shows no optical activity either way). (c) Y: SN2 attack from the back side gives inversion of configuration.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text:
The reaction of amines with mineral acids to form ammonium salts shows that they are basic. Aliphatic amines are stronger bases than ammonia, whereas aromatic amines are weaker. Primary and secondary amines react with acid chlorides, anhydrides and esters by nucleophilic substitution. A problem in electrophilic substitution of aromatic amines is their high reactivity; substitution occurs at ortho and para positions. The Hinsberg reagent distinguishes primary, secondary and tertiary amines. Aryldiazonium salts, obtained from arylamines, undergo replacement of the diazonium group by many nucleophiles, giving aryl halides, cyanides, phenols and arenes.

(i) Why is CH₃–NH₂ a stronger base than (CH₃)₃N in aqueous solution? (ii) Write structural formulae of A and B: CH₃CONH₂ —NaOBr→ A —C₆H₅COCl, base→ B
questions.solution: (i) In water, basicity depends on solvation of the ammonium ion as well as the +I effect. CH₃NH₃⁺ has three N–H hydrogens for hydrogen bonding with water, while (CH₃)₃NH⁺ has one and is crowded, so it is less stabilised. (ii) Hofmann bromamide: A = CH₃NH₂ (methanamine). Benzoylation: B = C₆H₅CONHCH₃ (N-methylbenzamide).

A compound X with molecular formula C₃H₉N reacts with Hinsberg reagent to give a product insoluble in alkali. Identify X.
questions.solution: An alkali-insoluble sulphonamide means a secondary amine: X is N-methylethanamine, CH₃CH₂NHCH₃.

How can you convert aniline to benzonitrile?
questions.solution: Diazotise aniline (NaNO₂/HCl, 0–5 °C) to benzenediazonium chloride, then treat with CuCN (Sandmeyer reaction) to get C₆H₅CN.

Why is the –NH₂ group of aniline acetylated before carrying out nitration?
questions.solution: Acetylation reduces the strong activating effect of –NH₂, prevents oxidation and anilinium ion formation by the nitrating mixture, and gives the p-nitro product mainly.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text:
Valence bond theory (VBT) explains the formation, magnetic behaviour and geometry of coordination compounds. Crystal field theory (CFT) is based on the effect of the crystal field of the ligands (taken as point charges) on the degeneracy of the d-orbital energies of the central metal atom or ion. The splitting of the d-orbitals gives different electronic arrangements in strong and weak crystal fields.

In an octahedral crystal field, the energies of which d-orbitals will be raised when ligands approach the central metal atom/ion? Give reason in support of your answer.
questions.solution: The e_g set (d(x²−y²) and d(z²)) is raised, because these orbitals point directly along the axes towards the approaching ligands and are repelled more. The t₂g set (dxy, dyz, dxz), pointing between the axes, is lowered.

The splitting of the d-orbitals gives different electronic arrangements in strong and weak crystal fields.

Using crystal field theory, write the electronic configuration of the central metal ion of (i) [CoF₆]³⁻ (ii) [Co(NH₃)₆]³⁺. [At. No. : Co = 27]
questions.solution: Co³⁺ is d⁶. (i) F⁻ is weak field: t₂g⁴ e_g² (high spin). (ii) NH₃ is strong field here: t₂g⁶ e_g⁰ (low spin).

[NiCl₄]²⁻ is paramagnetic while [Ni(CO)₄] is diamagnetic though both are tetrahedral. Why? [At. No. : Ni = 28]
questions.solution: In [NiCl₄]²⁻, Ni²⁺ (3d⁸) has two unpaired electrons, as weak-field Cl⁻ cannot pair them. In [Ni(CO)₄], Ni(0) is 3d⁸4s²; strong-field CO pairs all the electrons into 3d¹⁰, so it is diamagnetic.

Write the hybridisation and magnetic behaviour of the complex [Fe(CN)₆]³⁻. [Atomic No. : Fe = 26]
questions.solution: Fe³⁺ (3d⁵) with strong-field CN⁻ pairs into t₂g⁵: d²sp³ hybridisation, with one unpaired electron, so it is paramagnetic.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text:
(i) An organic compound X has the molecular formula C₅H₁₀O. Draw structures for X if it (I) does not give Tollens' test but gives a positive iodoform test (II) does not give Tollens' test or iodoform test but undergoes aldol condensation (III) undergoes Cannizzaro's reaction.
(ii) Show how each of the following compounds can be converted to benzoic acid : (I) Acetophenone (II) Ethylbenzene
questions.solution: (i) (I) A methyl ketone: pentan-2-one, CH₃COCH₂CH₂CH₃ (or 3-methylbutan-2-one). (II) A ketone with α-H but not a methyl ketone: pentan-3-one, CH₃CH₂COCH₂CH₃. (III) An aldehyde with no α-H: 2,2-dimethylpropanal, (CH₃)₃CCHO. (ii) (I) Iodoform reaction: C₆H₅COCH₃ + NaOI → C₆H₅COONa + CHI₃, then acidify. (II) Oxidise with alkaline KMnO₄ (heat), then acidify: C₆H₅CH₂CH₃ → C₆H₅COOH.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: Answer the following : (i) Write the structure of the 2,4-dinitrophenylhydrazone derivative of benzaldehyde. (ii) Arrange in increasing order of reactivity towards HCN : di-tert-butyl ketone, acetaldehyde, acetone. (iii) Give a simple chemical test to distinguish between benzoic acid and ethyl benzoate. (iv) Name the reagent to convert ethanenitrile to ethanal. (v) Write the product X when cyclohexanol is treated with CrO₃.
questions.solution: (i) C₆H₅CH=N–NH–C₆H₃(NO₂)₂ (the NO₂ groups at positions 2 and 4 of the ring). (ii) Di-tert-butyl ketone < acetone < acetaldehyde. (iii) Sodium bicarbonate test: benzoic acid gives brisk effervescence of CO₂; ethyl benzoate does not. (iv) SnCl₂/HCl followed by hydrolysis (Stephen reduction), or DIBAL-H then H₂O. (v) Cyclohexanone.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text:
(i) From the following E°(M²⁺/M) values: V −1.18, Cr −0.91, Mn −1.18, Fe −0.44, Co −0.28, Ni −0.25, Cu +0.34 V, answer: (I) Why do the E°(M²⁺/M) values show an irregular trend? (II) Why is E°(Cu²⁺/Cu) exceptionally positive? (III) Why is E°(Mn²⁺/Mn) highly negative?
(ii) Write the ionic equations for the oxidising action of potassium permanganate in its reaction with I⁻ in both acidic and alkaline solutions.
questions.solution: (i)(I) The values depend on enthalpy of atomisation, ionisation enthalpies and hydration enthalpy, which vary irregularly across the series. (II) Copper's high atomisation and ionisation enthalpies are not compensated by its hydration enthalpy. (III) Mn²⁺ has the stable half-filled 3d⁵ configuration. (ii) Acidic: 2MnO₄⁻ + 10I⁻ + 16H⁺ → 2Mn²⁺ + 5I₂ + 8H₂O. Alkaline/neutral: 2MnO₄⁻ + I⁻ + H₂O → 2MnO₂ + IO₃⁻ + 2OH⁻.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: Answer the following : (i) Name a member of the lanthanoid series which exhibits (I) the +4 oxidation state (II) the +2 oxidation state. (ii) Why do transition metals act as good catalysts? (iii) Why does Cr have a higher melting point than Mn? (iv) What happens when an acidic solution of potassium permanganate is allowed to stand for some time? Give the equation involved. What is this type of reaction called?
questions.solution: (i)(I) Cerium (Ce⁴⁺). (II) Europium (Eu²⁺) or ytterbium (Yb²⁺). (ii) They show variable oxidation states and can form unstable intermediates, and they provide a surface for adsorption of reactants. (iii) Cr (3d⁵4s¹) has more unpaired electrons available for strong metallic bonding; in Mn the stable 3d⁵ set holds electrons less available for bonding. (iv) It slowly decomposes: 4MnO₄⁻ + 4H⁺ → 4MnO₂ + 3O₂ + 2H₂O. This is a redox (autocatalytic decomposition) reaction, catalysed by MnO₂ formed.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: For the reaction 2AgCl(s) + H₂(g) (0.4 atm) → 2Ag(s) + 2H⁺ (0.1 M) + 2Cl⁻ (0.2 M), calculate the emf of the cell at 25 °C. Given : ΔG° = −43500 J mol⁻¹. [log 10 = 1, 1 F = 96500 C mol⁻¹]
